title: subak --json output, schema_version 1
description: Every document `subak ... --json` prints (Step 12; capture, history and clear-history since Step 13; the `hotkeys` group since Step 17, whose data hotkeys-cli-v1 specifies; the `config` and `profile` groups and `new --profile` since Step 20; docs/SUBAK_CLI.md, docs/CLI_CONTRACT.md): the cli-envelope-v1 envelope, the `data` of each command (selected by `command`; the deprecated `subak terminal <verb>` spelling reports the canonical name), and Subak's error-code registry with its exit codes. Terminal objects are the ipc-v1 definitions, copied verbatim (a test keeps them identical); the capabilities document is tool-capabilities-v1. Objects are closed so regression tests notice any change; consumers must still ignore unknown fields and tolerate new enum values (CLI_CONTRACT §8).

ssh_plan.description: Step 34 (ADR 0067): how the SSH pane connects — Windows' OpenSSH client with strict host keys and no agent forwarding; whether the destination is in known_hosts and a saved secret answers the password or passphrase prompt (never the secret itself; `env` lists names only).

warnings.description: Step 35: what the user must know (agent or X11 forwarding, a forward beyond loopback); also printed on stderr.

login_script_result.description: Step 35: what a login script did, step by step (the text sent is never a secret).

skipped.description: Links and special files that were not copied.

transfer_job.description: Step 35: a background transfer (`%APPDATA%\mouv\subak\transfers\<id>.json`); never a secret.

telnet_plan.description: Step 36 (ADR 0069): a Telnet pane — off by default, always warned about.

serial_plan.description: Step 36: a serial pane's line settings.

ok_bridge_connect.description: Step 36: `subak telnet connect` / `subak serial connect` — the `new` result of a Terminal whose pane runs Subak's Telnet or serial bridge.

ok_serial_list.description: Step 36: `subak serial list` — the serial ports Windows lists (read only).

ok_ssh_hosts.description: Step 36: `subak ssh hosts` — the concrete Host entries of an ssh config (read only).

ok_sftp_ls.description: Step 35: `subak sftp ls <dest> [<path>]` — the directory as the server lists it.

ok_sftp_transfer.description: Step 35: `subak sftp get|put` — the finished transfer (`result`), its dry run, or with --background the queued job.

ok_ssh_connect.description: Step 34: `subak ssh connect <[user@]host[:port]> [<name>]` — the `new` result of a Terminal whose pane runs ssh, with `ssh`.

ok_ssh_credential.description: Step 34: `subak ssh credential status|save|forget <[user@]host[:port]>` — the Credential Manager entry, whether a secret is saved and whether the host is in known_hosts. Never the secret.

ok_shell_integration.description: Step 33: `subak shell-integration status|install|uninstall [powershell|pwsh|cmd]` — the PowerShell profile file and whether Subak's block is in it (install and uninstall: what changed and the backup written first); cmd: the per-profile opt-in, nothing installed.

restore_plan.description: Step 30 (ADR 0064): what restoring a saved Terminal does pane by pane, and what cannot come back.

would_create_pane.description: Step 21: what window.create (window_id null; the new window's index and name) or pane.create (the window it goes into) would start.

split.description: Step 22: pane.split only: the pane it splits and how.

selection.description: Step 21: the selection window.select or pane.select made (or would make): the window, its active pane, and whether anything changed.

close_plan.description: Step 21: what window.kill or pane.kill ends (also the details of its `busy` refusal).

result_window_create.description: Step 21: the result of window.create, pane.create and (Step 22) pane.split: the new pane, the window that holds it, and whether it became the active one.

result_layout.description: Step 22: the result of pane.adjust (moved: cells the border moved), pane.swap, pane.zoom, window.rotate and window.select_layout: the window's layout afterwards; with dry_run, the layout it would have.

buffer_info.description: Step 24: one paste buffer as listed: never its text, a redacted first line only.

result_buffer_list.description: Step 24: buffer.list (tmux list-buffers), newest first; buffers live in the Host's memory only.

result_buffer_get.description: Step 24: buffer.get (tmux show-buffer): one buffer's text.

result_buffer_set.description: Step 24: buffer.set (tmux set-buffer); with dry_run, what would be kept.

result_buffer_delete.description: Step 24: buffer.delete (tmux delete-buffer); with dry_run, which buffer would go.

result_input.description: Step 24: pane.send_keys and buffer.paste: the bytes written to the pane as input (never echoed back); with dry_run, what would be.

result_move_pane.description: Step 24: pane.break (tmux break-pane: a new window holds the pane) and pane.join (join-pane: the pane joined window_id; window_removed when its old window went with it).

state_terminal.description: Step 29: a saved Terminal as `subak state` shows it; `missing` lists working directories and absolute program paths that no longer exist (reported, never acted on).

ok_state_show.description: Step 29: `subak state show|check` — state.json read without changing anything (ADR 0063).

ok_state_backups.description: Step 29: `subak state backups` — newest first, at most 5.

ok_state_change.description: Step 29: `subak state forget|policy` — done by the running Host (`via: host`) or, without one, in the file (`via: file`, a backup first).

ok_state_rollback.description: Step 29: `subak state rollback [backup]` (no Host may run): the backup made current; the file it replaced is kept as state.before-rollback-<time>.json.

ok_claude_hooks_status.description: Step 27: `subak claude hooks status` — whether Subak's hook is in each Claude Code event of the settings file.

ok_claude_hooks_change.description: Step 27: `subak claude hooks install|uninstall` — the events Subak's hook was added to or removed from, and the backup written first (null: no file before, a dry run, or nothing to change).

ok_claude_report.description: Step 27: `subak claude report` (run by a Claude Code hook; always exit 0): whether the event reached the pane's Host. Only ids, the event and the state — never hook input content.

result_command.description: Step 24: `subak command` (tmux command lines): each command's IPC method and its result, in order; or, with --dry-run, the plan.

result_topology.description: Step 21: the result of window.list (every window) and pane.list (every window, or the one targeted, with its panes).

claude_state.description: Step 28: the Terminal's Claude Code state, the most urgent of its panes' sessions (need-input > error > done > in-progress > unknown > idle > none); from hooks only. Hosts before Step 28 omit it.

last_window.description: Step 25: the previously active window (tmux last-window, {last}); null when none. Hosts before Step 25 omit it.

result_select.description: Step 21: the result of window.select and pane.select.

result_close.description: Step 21: the result of window.kill and pane.kill: one report per ended pane; `terminal` is the Terminal afterwards.

ok_hotkeys.description: `subak hotkeys ...` (Step 17): the data is specified by hotkeys-cli-v1 (list_data, show_data, change_data, check_data, export_data), as for `kim hotkeys` and `noeul hotkeys`.

command_name.description: Dotted command path, e.g. `catalog.list`; the tool name alone (e.g. `kim`) when the arguments could not be parsed.

allOf.description: Destructive commands need --yes when the tool cannot ask.

capabilities.description: The `data` of `<tool> capabilities --json`, and the optional `capabilities.json` manifest at the root of an installed version (docs/CLI_CONTRACT.md §9). Every command that is not `read` supports --dry-run; every `destructive` command needs --yes when the tool cannot ask. The same definitions are embedded in kim-cli-v1 (a test keeps them identical).

terminal_name.description: A Terminal name (docs/SESSION_MODEL.md §3); the Host enforces the full rules.

env_names.description: The names (never the values) of a pane's environment overrides (Step 11, docs/PTY_PROCESSES.md).

pane.description: A pane of a Terminal object: stored fields (STATE_SCHEMA.md) plus volatile ones.

current_dir.description: Step 33: the directory the shell reported last (OSC 7 or 9;9, with an optional shell integration); null when it never did.

command_line.description: Step 12: the verbatim command line the pane was started with (terminal.create command_line, host serve --shell), with secret-looking words as ***; null when command was quoted word by word. Hosts before Step 12 omit it.

executable.description: The program file that runs (command.program resolved on the pane's PATH); null before it started.

rect.description: Step 22: the pane's place in its window's layout (the whole window while it is zoomed). Hosts before Step 22 omit it.

visible.description: Step 22: false while another pane of the window is zoomed. Hosts before Step 22 omit it.

history.description: Step 13: the pane's history counters while the Host keeps its screen (also for a stopped Terminal); null before it started. Hosts before Step 13 omit it.

Step 13 (docs/SCROLLBACK.md): numbers about a pane's history, never its content. Lines are rows that scrolled off the top of the primary screen; the oldest are evicted first once either limit is reached.

size.description: Step 22: the window's size (the latest interactive client's); its panes share it. Hosts before Step 22 omit it.

zoomed.description: Step 22: the zoomed pane, which fills the window while the others keep their places unseen; null when none. Hosts before Step 22 omit it.

options.description: Step 25: the window's tmux options. Hosts before Step 25 omit it.

activity.description: Step 25: output while the window was not shown (monitor-activity).

bell.description: Step 25: a bell while the window was not shown (monitor-bell).

layout.description: Step 22 (ADR 0056): a window's split tree. A horizontal split puts its children side by side (tmux -h), a vertical one stacks them (tmux -v); siblings are one cell apart. size is a child's share of its split (0-1), cells its extent along the split.

rect.description: Step 22: where a pane is in its window, in cells from the window's top-left corner.

terminal.description: The Terminal object of terminal.info, terminal.list (detail full), terminal.create and terminal.created.

claude_state.description: Step 28: the Terminal's Claude Code state, the most urgent of its panes' sessions (need-input > error > done > in-progress > unknown > idle > none); from hooks only. Hosts before Step 28 omit it.

last_window.description: Step 25: the previously active window (tmux last-window, {last}); null when none. Hosts before Step 25 omit it.

terminal_summary.description: A Terminal in terminal.list with detail summary (the default).

claude_state.description: Step 28: the Terminal's Claude Code state, the most urgent of its panes' sessions; from hooks only. Hosts before Step 28 omit it.

pane_end_report.description: How one pane's processes ended (terminal.stop/kill/remove, host.stop).

result_terminal_end.description: The result of terminal.stop, terminal.kill and terminal.remove.

client_attachment.description: One attachment client.detach ends (or would end).

detach_terminal.description: The Terminal a client.detach target resolved to, or null without a target.

screen_info.description: Step 13: the pane's screen as the Host's terminal model has it.

result_pane_capture.description: Step 13: pane.capture. Line numbers: screen rows from 0, history lines from -1 (newest) down; start and end are those captured (null when the range was empty). Lines are redacted unless redact is false; redacted counts hidden values. truncated: older lines were left out to fit one message; capture again with an earlier end.

result_pane_clear_history.description: Step 13: pane.clear_history. Only the Host's copy is cleared; the screen stays.

scrollback.description: Step 13: host.status scrollback: what the Host keeps of terminal output (in its memory only; never on disk).

error_code.description: Every error code subak reports (docs/CLI_CONTRACT.md §6; crates/subak/src/output.rs). The `hotkey*` and `action_not_found` codes come from the `subak hotkeys` group (Step 17), whose documents follow hotkeys-cli-v1. The `config_*`, `profile_not_found` and `secret_in_config` codes come from the `config` and `profile` groups and `new --profile` (Step 20).

job.description: The limits of the job a process runs in (risk R-03), or null outside any job.

initial_pane.description: host.status pane: the Terminal the Host was started with (--shell) while it exists.

data_new.description: new: the terminal.create result plus host {pid, started}, or a dry run (with or without a Host); since Step 20 with `profile`.

profile.description: Step 20: the shell profile of config.toml that was used (--profile or the default profile); absent when none was.
Step 20: the shell profile of config.toml that was used (--profile or the default profile); absent when none was.

data_status.description: status: the Host, every Terminal and every client; running false (and nulls) when no Host serves the endpoint.

data_attach.description: attach / host attach: only a dry run prints a document (the real attach streams the terminal).

data_detach.description: detach: the client.detach result plus host {pid}. Detaching never stops a process.

data_host_serve.description: host serve: the final report when the Host ends, or a dry run.

data_history.description: history: what the Host keeps of one Terminal's output (numbers only, never content): its history counters and limits and its screen. Kept in the Host's memory only, never on disk (docs/SCROLLBACK.md).

data_capture.description: capture: pane.capture with every page joined (truncated is then false unless --max-lines cut it), plus the Terminal's name and how many requests it took.

data_clear_history.description: clear-history: pane.clear_history plus the Terminal's name; or a dry run.

ok_config_check.description: Step 20: `subak config check`: exits 0; `valid` says whether every value was used.

ok_config_export.description: Step 20: `subak config export`: the file (or the defaults) with secret-looking values replaced by ***.

config_state.description: How config.toml was found: missing (the defaults), user (read), invalid (not TOML or not a settings document; the defaults apply, never rewritten by an edit), newer (written by a newer Subak; read-only), unreadable.

key.description: section.name, profiles[i].field, or empty for the whole file.

line.description: The 1-based line in config.toml, when known.

severity.description: error: the value (or profile) is not used and its default applies; warning: used, but worth fixing (a secret-looking value, a default profile that does not exist).

config_profile.description: A shell profile as Subak shows it (subak-config-v1 $defs/profile): values that look secret are ***.

unknown.description: Keys this build does not know; kept as they are.

backups.description: The folder of the backups that reset --all and import keep (the newest 5).

before.description: The value before (TOML text; null: not in the file, so the default applied).

after.description: The value after (null: removed, so the default applies).

backup.description: The copy of the previous file (reset --all, import), if one was made.

from.description: import: the file that was imported.

source.description: file: the file as it is; defaults: there is no file.

redacted.description: How many secret-looking values were replaced by ***.
